The recurring trigger

A supplier statement is only the start.

Recurring purchases can reuse yesterday’s paperwork while production facts change. A checklist should distinguish documents on file from evidence actually reviewed for a specific claim.

Required inputs

  • Production and supplier facts
  • Origin statements and relevant certifications
  • Program-specific preference evidence

Prepared output

  • SKU and supplier evidence checklist
  • Missing, contradictory, or unreviewed proof
  • Owner, due date, and review notes

A specific review sequence

Make each step inspectable.

01

Define the evidence needed

Separate origin evidence from preference-program requirements.

02

Identify what is missing

Give each absent or inconsistent document an owner and next action.

03

Review the stated purpose

Record what the evidence supports, and what remains unassessed.

01 / Inside the proposed module

One SKU can have several supplier stories.

Evidence is linked to the supplier and production facts. A new supplier or process change should trigger a fresh review rather than inherit a blanket status.

Inspect the synthetic example

02 / Inside the proposed module

A hold is useful information.

HX-42 is held because ORG-HX42-v1 is absent. Loading a fictional response in the demo does not make it reviewed or prove preference eligibility.

Inspect the synthetic example

03 / Inside the proposed module

Dates belong with the proof.

Show when evidence was published, the period it concerns, and when it was retrieved. These dates answer different questions.

Inspect the synthetic example

Controls & scope

What the output
can—and cannot—settle.

An available document or a completed checklist does not establish origin or preference eligibility. Applicable rules and production facts require human assessment.

Expected reviewer: importer compliance owner and customs broker; counsel where the question requires it.

Review the limits

The pilot question

Would this help the
broker prepare the entry?

Origin and valuation gaps found, unresolved holds, and the broker’s acceptance of the evidence for its stated purpose.

Discuss offer 2

Before the next step

Questions for this offer.

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Does a complete checklist prove eligibility?

No. Completeness and eligibility are separate review questions. Program-specific rules and production evidence still need assessment.

What happens when proof is missing?

The gap remains held with an owner and due date. The demo cannot turn an absent document into verified evidence.
